heading: Frequently Asked Questions
desc: Let's find the answers to your questions.
a_why_vpnhood: VpnHood is powered by the VpnHood! ENGINE, developed by the VpnHood team. It combines open-source client and server code, flexible split tunneling and Cloak Mode, which is designed to help VPN traffic blend into ordinary encrypted browsing. VpnHood! CONNECT offers unlimited free data without account registration on Android.
a_is_vpnhood_free: Yes, VpnHood offers a free VPN service without any time, data, or speed limitations. However, you can unlock additional features by upgrading to a premium subscription. With the premium plan, you gain access to servers in more countries, faster connection speeds, and enhanced app functionality. For further information, visit the plan details page.
a_connect_vs_client: VpnHood! CONNECT is a free VPN that users can enjoy without limitations. However, while VpnHood! CLIENT is also free, it does not include servers for direct connections. It connects to a VpnHood! server that you, or someone you trust, already runs, using an access key they give you.
a_supported_platforms: VpnHood! CLIENT runs on Android, iOS (iPhone and iPad), Windows, and Linux. VpnHood! CONNECT runs on Android, iOS (iPhone and iPad), Windows, and Linux. On iOS, Windows and Linux, VpnHood! CONNECT has no free servers; you'll need to purchase a Premium Key, which is available on the pricing page.
a_is_open_source: Yes, all of it. VpnHood! CONNECT, VpnHood! CLIENT, the server, and the VpnHood! ENGINE behind them are published on GitHub, and the project has been audited by Include Security for the Open Technology Fund's Red Team Lab. You can read the code yourself rather than take our word for it.
a_is_undetectable: VpnHood's Cloak Mode is designed to make VPN traffic resemble ordinary HTTPS traffic, helping it avoid some VPN-detection methods. This does not guarantee that every network will allow the connection; effectiveness depends on the filtering methods in use.
q_stay_free_forever: Can I stay on the free plan forever?
a_stay_free_forever: Yes. The free plan has no time limit and no forced upgrade, and there is no account to create. It is funded by ads, so it is not available in China or in other countries where ads are not served. Premium is there when you want more locations, faster servers, an ad-free app and 24/7 support, and it has no such limit.
q_free_data_cap: Is there a data cap on the free plan?
a_free_data_cap: No. The free plan has no data cap and no time limit. The VpnHood! server can enforce a monthly quota per user, and on the free servers none is set, so nothing counts down while you browse. Most free VPNs cap you at a few gigabytes because the cap is what sells the upgrade.
q_free_speed: Do you slow down free users?
a_free_speed: No. The VpnHood! server can cap speed per user, and on the free servers it does not. What differs between the plans is capacity: free servers carry many more people, so your share of a server changes with how busy it is, while Premium servers are more powerful and shared only among premium users, which is why they are consistently faster.
q_why_slower: Why is VpnHood! slower than my normal connection?
a_why_slower: Every VPN costs some speed: your data is encrypted and travels through one more machine before it reaches the site you asked for. Distance is usually the bigger factor, so a nearer server helps most. Cloak Mode and Smart Proxies each add overhead and can be turned off when nothing is blocking you. See the speed testing guide for how to measure it properly.
q_request_location: Can I ask for a new location?
a_request_location: Yes. Locations are added where demand shows up, and requests are how we see it. Use the contact page, name the country, and say whether you need it for speed or to reach something specific, because that changes where the server should be.
q_many_servers_per_location: Is each location a single server?
a_many_servers_per_location: No. Every location is a group of servers, not one machine. You pick the country and the app picks the server inside it, going for the fastest one it can reach, so you never have to compare individual servers yourself. See every location.
q_reseller_program: What is a VPN reseller program?
a_reseller_program: It lets you sell a VPN service without building one. The provider supplies the technology, the apps and the servers; you handle pricing, marketing and your own customers. With VpnHood! what you buy and resell is an access code, so there is no infrastructure for you to run and nothing to develop.
a_reseller_open_source: Because your customers can check it. VpnHood! CONNECT, the server and the VpnHood! ENGINE behind them are published on GitHub under the LGPL, and Include Security has audited them for the Open Technology Fund's Red Team Lab. A closed VPN asks buyers to trust a promise; this one lets them read the code, which makes the sale easier and the support questions fewer.
q_reseller_app_cost: Do my customers pay for the app?
a_reseller_app_cost: No. VpnHood! CONNECT is a free download on Android, iOS, Windows and Linux. On Android it also has free servers funded by ads, so people can try it before they buy. On iOS, Windows and Linux there are no free servers, so your customers need a paid plan to connect, and the access code for that plan is what you sell.
a_audit_independent: Yes. Include Security reviewed the Android app, the Windows app and the VPN server, in an engagement commissioned and paid for by the Open Technology Fund's Red Team Lab. The report was published in full.
q_audit_who_paid: Who paid for the VpnHood! security audit?
a_audit_who_paid: The Open Technology Fund commissioned the engagement and paid for it, not us. The firm doing the reviewing was not being paid by the people being reviewed, which is the part that makes a finding worth something.
q_audit_findings: Did the audit find any serious vulnerabilities?
a_audit_findings: No critical or high-risk issues were found. There was one medium-risk finding, about how the Android app was signed for older Android versions, and three informational ones. All four, and our response to each, are in the published report.
a_server_free: Yes, and open source under the LGPL. The only cost is the machine you run it on, rented from any provider you like.
q_server_requirements: What do I need to run a VpnHood! server?
a_server_requirements: A VPS or a dedicated machine running Linux (x64 or ARM64) or Windows, or any host that runs Docker. It uses port 443 by default and needs no other network configuration.
q_server_needs_manager: Do I need VpnHood! MANAGER to run a server?
a_server_needs_manager: No. VpnHood! SERVER ships with a small built-in file-based access manager, so one server can run and issue its own keys with no panel at all. MANAGER is what you add when you want a dashboard, live monitoring, your own plans, and several servers sharing the load.
q_server_ip_blocked: Can my server's IP address still be blocked?
a_server_ip_blocked: Yes. Cloak Mode leaves little in the traffic to fingerprint, so what usually gets a server blocked is its IP address. Keep it private and share it with few people. With MANAGER, on supported hosts, you can order a fresh IP and release the old one, and your users' apps pick up the change on their own.
